tools.name: billetweb_list_events
tools.description: List the organiser's events with id, name, start/end, place, shop URL, online state, tax rate, tags and contact. Past events are left out unless include_past is set. GET /events.

tools.name: billetweb_get_availability
tools.description: Remaining places of an event: per session, per category and per ticket type, with avail (-1 = unlimited), quota and sales. Use it to answer 'how many seats are left'. GET /event/{id}/avail.

tools.name: billetweb_list_tickets
tools.description: The ticket types (tarifs) of an event in display order: id, name, price, category, quota, visibility (0 visible, 1 web, 2 box office, 3 secret link, 4 hidden), sales window, tax and commission. GET /event/{id}/tickets.

tools.name: billetweb_list_sessions
tools.description: The sessions (séances, dates) of a multi-session event: id, start/end, name, place, quota, total_sales, state (0 open, 1 hidden, 2 box office only, 3 web only, 4 link only, 5 cancelled) and the ticket ids sold in it. GET /event/{id}/dates.

tools.name: billetweb_list_attendees
tools.description: The attendees (one row per ticket) of one event: name, email, ticket type, price, check-in state (used), session, order id and payment, custom form answers. Filter by session, ticket, buyer, check-in state or when the order changed; use updated_since to fetch only what is new. Billetweb allows 10 at

tools.name: billetweb_list_all_attendees
tools.description: The attendees of ALL events, newest changes included, with the same fields as billetweb_list_attendees. Filter by event tag, only unfinished events, buyer, ticket, check-in state or order change time. Billetweb allows 10 attendees calls per minute; use updated_since for incremental reads. GET /atten

tools.name: billetweb_list_waiting_list
tools.description: People on the waiting list of an event: name, email, phone, ticket/session wanted, places asked for and whether they were notified. GET /event/{id}/waiting.

tools.name: billetweb_list_accounting
tools.description: The accounting history: one row per ticket and per money movement, type product_pay (sale) or product_refund (negative price), with price incl. tax, Billetweb fees, tax, payment type, transaction id and payout id (0 = not paid out yet). Period at most 1 year, starting at most 1 year ago. GET /accoun

tools.name: billetweb_list_payouts
tools.description: The bank transfers Billetweb made to the organiser (type out) or took back (type in, negative amount): id, date, net amount, account holder. The IBAN is masked to its last 4 characters. GET /payouts.

tools.name: billetweb_get_payout
tools.description: The line-by-line detail of one payout: each sale, refund or transfer with ticket reference, order, event, price, fees and tax. Net transferred = sum of price minus sum of fees. Pass a payout id, or a date (yyyy-mm-dd) for all payouts of that day. GET /payout/{id}/data.

tools.name: billetweb_list_crm_contacts
tools.description: The organiser's buyer contacts: name, email, first/last purchase, number of orders and tickets, total spent and average ticket price. Filter by email, CRM segment or last change. GET /crm/contacts.

tools.name: billetweb_list_crm_segments
tools.description: The saved CRM segments (id, name, created, last sync). Use an id as the segment filter of billetweb_list_crm_contacts. GET /crm/segments.

tools.name: billetweb_list_lists
tools.description: The organiser's custom lists (id, name, key type), such as member or invitation lists used for access control and discounts. GET /lists.

tools.name: billetweb_get_list_data
tools.description: The rows of one custom list (each row is an array of values, the first being the key). GET /list/{id}/data.

tools.name: billetweb_check_tickets
tools.description: WRITE: set the check-in state of tickets (composter): 1 = checked in, 2 = checked out, 0 = back to not checked in. tools.description: WRITE: confirm the payment of reservation orders (unpaid orders taken as a reservation) with the payment type you were given (card, cash, check, reservation, other). findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "billetweb_list_tickets" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: The ticket types (tarifs) of an event in display order: id, name, price, category, quota, visibility (0 visible, 1 web, 2 box office, 3 secret link, 4 hidden), …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: billetweb_list_events, billetweb_get_availability, billetweb_list_tickets, billetweb_list_sessions, billetweb_list_attendees, billetweb_list_all_attendees, billetweb_list_waiting_list, billetweb_list_accounting, billetweb_get_payout, billetweb_list_crm_contacts, billetweb_check_tickets, billetweb_mark_orders_paid, billetweb_send_payment_requests, billetweb_create_offline_orders · Private data: billetweb_list_events, billetweb_list_tickets, billetweb_list_crm_contacts · Public sink: billetweb_list_attendees, billetweb_list_waiting_list, billetweb_list_crm_contacts, billetweb_check_tickets, billetweb_mark_orders_paid, billetweb_send_payment_requests, billetweb_create_offline_orders.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: billetweb_list_events, billetweb_get_availability, billetweb_list_tickets, billetweb_list_sessions, billetweb_list_attendees, billetweb_list_all_attendees, billetweb_list_waiting_list, billetweb_list_accounting, billetweb_get_payout, billetweb_list_crm_contacts, billetweb_check_tickets, billetweb_mark_orders_paid, billetweb_send_payment_requests, billetweb_create_offline_orders · Private data: billetweb_list_events, billetweb_list_tickets, billetweb_list_crm_contacts · Public sink: billetweb_list_attendees, billetweb_list_waiting_list, billetweb_list_crm_contacts, billetweb_check_tickets, billetweb_mark_orders_paid, billetweb_send_payment_requests, billetweb_create_offline_orders

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
